title: Prevent partial Event Search results when a second source is revoked during a completed Case hunt
goal: Verify the actual first-party Event Search Job refuses the entire response when an in-window but nonmatching source is revoked, or the request is cancelled, after an earlier authorized result. Close a real source-auth fail-closed coverage gap without changing product semantics or bypassing mandatory runtime coverage.
invariants: An owner-authorized earlier Search Job hit is never serialized if any subsequent in-window imported source becomes unavailable.
An unrelated nonmatching imported source must STILL undergo owner typed-source authorization before family/text filtering.
No partial first-party results, source IDs, raw preview or bearer on failed/cancelled request.
No weakening of mandatory security coverage floor or change to existing Case, Timeline or SearchJob schemas.
security_properties: Server owner reauthorizes every relevant candidate, not the browser or client payload.
Test a real completed first-party successful source hunt as positive control.
Revoked source and cancelled request must return no Search Job or partial result.

migration.rationale: Only regression test and explicit handoff, no runtime contract, persistence or schema change.

rollback.strategy: Remove only the new integration regression test; existing first-party source validation and checks remain.
verification: Previously successful runtime Go+Node and cross-OS tests still run.

inputs: Existing Case/Timeline owner and normalized offline imported-event first-party Event Search Job
Changed-security-critical runtime Go coverage fallback on PR #135 is 89.30% under unchanged mandatory 90%.
outputs: A real two-event, in-window Search Job with an earlier match and later benign non-match.
Source owner revocation or request cancellation at the second typed-source opening denies the ENTIRE Job; no partial ref leakage.
Exact GitHub SHA and CI evidence, distinguishing functional gate vs release gate.
acceptance_tests: Positive-control actual POST /demo-local-search returns exactly one previously owner-authorized result.
When the second, nonmatching source is revoked during the same request, the HTTP search fails and discloses no prior hit or metadata.
When context is cancelled during second source resolution, the HTTP search fails without partially completed Job.
linux Go/Node and macOS/Windows runtime CI and 90% security coverage checked without waiver.

performance_budget.rationale: No runtime behavior changed, one bounded deterministic two-event regression.

definition_of_ready: Canonical Class-0 Search Job must remain permission-aware and source-scoped; parent E10-INV-002G and E10-INV-110E were marked VERIFIED; no OPEN decision is assumed resolved.
Explicit new engineering unit rather than reclassifying E10-INV-110G frontend selector or altering its frozen SHA.
Existing owner services and test fixtures suffice, no new production interfaces.
definition_of_done: A real first-party Search Job suite documents the revocation and cancellation property.
PR is published as draft based on frozen #135 and all exact-head required checks read.
Unit is never marked VERIFIED or parent accepted with mandatory coverage below 90% or outstanding native approvals.
